questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question probes designing a scalable, extensible command-dispatch system with runtime pluggability, ordering guarantees, and per-handler policies.

## Key Concepts
- Command Pattern and Mediator
- Runtime registries and type-safe dispatch
- Per-type queuing, concurrency, backpressure
- Policy hooks (retry, concurrency) and isolation

## Code Example
```javascript
interface Command { type: string; payload: any }
interface ICommandHandler { handle(cmd: Command): Promise<any> }
interface IPolicy { apply(context: any): void }
class Registry { register(type: string, h: ICommandHandler) { /* ... */ } lookup(type: string): ICommandHandler | undefined { /* ... */ } }
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you detect and prevent circular registrations?
- How would you test order guarantees under load?
- What are trade-offs vs a pure Mediator vs Event-driven approach?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Dynamic circuit-breaking with runtime rule extension is common in large-scale systems but hard to implement safely. This tests how a candidate balances performance, correctness, and distribution.

## Key Concepts
- Circuit-breaker state per endpoint
- Runtime registries and factories
- Distributed state and synchronization
- Testing concurrent trips and race conditions

## Code Example
```javascript
```javascript
interface CircuitBreakerRule {
  name: string
  shouldTrip(ctx: any): boolean
  onStateChange?(ctx: any): void
}
type RuleFactory = () => CircuitBreakerRule
class Registry {
  private map = new Map()
  register(name, factory){ this.map.set(name, factory) }
  create(name){ const f = this.map.get(name); return f ? f() : null }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you persist circuit-breaker state across a cluster?
- How would you test time-based thresholds and backoff without slowing tests?

## Why This Is Asked

Practical multi-tenant routing with runtime extensibility; assesses patterns and trade-offs.

## Key Concepts

- Strategy: channel dispatch per policy
- Registry: per-tenant policy storage
- Composite: policy groups with priorities
- Backpressure: async dispatch and rate limits

## Code Example

```javascript
// Interfaces sketch (simplified)
interface Channel { send(payload: any): Promise<void> }
interface Policy { evaluate(event: any): boolean; channels: string[]; priority: number }
interface PolicyRegistry { register(tenant: string, p: Policy): void; resolve(tenant: string, event: any): Policy[] }
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you ensure isolation across tenants during policy updates?
- How would you test performance under burst traffic?
